title: Automated Logistics Fleet Deployment
business: A regional logistics firm managing a fleet of autonomous delivery drones that requires frequent firmware updates to navigation software.
problem: Manual deployment processes lead to inconsistent firmware versions across the drone fleet, resulting in navigation errors and significant downtime during manual troubleshooting.
solution: GitLab CI/CD provides an integrated pipeline that enforces a standardized build, test, and deployment sequence, ensuring every firmware update is validated against automated test suites before being pushed to the fleet management server.
steps: Define a .gitlab-ci.yml file in the repository root to establish build, test, and deploy stages.
Configure GitLab Runners as execution agents to process the firmware compilation and unit testing tasks.
Utilize protected CI/CD variables to securely store API keys required for communicating with the fleet management server.
Implement pipeline stages to ensure that the deployment job only triggers if the test stage completes successfully.
Use CI/CD components to standardize the deployment logic across multiple drone model repositories.
outcome: A reliable, repeatable deployment process that eliminates configuration drift and ensures only verified firmware reaches the production drone fleet.
limitation: A primary limitation is the potential for pipeline bottlenecks if too many jobs are queued for a single runner; this can be checked by monitoring the job queue duration in the GitLab CI/CD pipeline dashboard.

diagram.description: The sequence of automated actions triggered by a code commit.

code.content:
stages:
  - build
  - test
  - deploy

build_firmware:
  stage: build
  script: make compile # Compiles the drone firmware

test_firmware:
  stage: test
  script: ./run_nav_tests.sh # Validates navigation logic

deploy_to_fleet:
  stage: deploy
  script: ./push_to_server.sh # Deploys to fleet management server
  variables:
    API_KEY: $SECURE_API_KEY # Uses protected variable for security
code.explanation: This configuration maps to the Automated Logistics Fleet Deployment scenario by defining the mandatory stages to ensure firmware is built, tested, and deployed in a controlled, secure manner.
